goal: Build named accepted-service cohorts, observed operating outputs, independent validation, and explicit closeout, performance, rate, capacity, and baseline holds from the Phase 57A handoff.
publication_rule: Publish only when the named entity and cohort have an observed turnover, accepted service, or operating output with explicit stage, period, unit, method, denominator, and attribution; retain forward schedules, reporting contracts, undisclosed performance, analytical capacity, and incomplete baselines as In Review.
authority_rule: Service availability is not adoption; turnover is not final outcome; analytical capacity is not recurring output; independent reporting is not causal validation.

reopened_holds.result: Partially reopened for one 104-location Nextlink service-availability cohort; the broader nearly 5,000-location authorization cohort remains open.

records.title: Amtrak turns over eleven station projects for passenger use in the six-month cohort
records.finding: Amtrak reports that eleven named stations reached substantial completion between November 1, 2025 and April 30, 2026; its definition says primary scope was complete and the facilities were turned over for passenger use.
records.denominator: Eleven named station projects in Amtrak's November 1, 2025 through April 30, 2026 construction cohort: Camden, Detroit Lakes, Du Quoin, Fort Morgan, Granby, Hamlet, Havre, Miami, Pomona, Rocklin, and Rugby.
evidence_limits: Substantial completion can leave punch-list or minor work outstanding.
Passenger-use turnover does not establish station-feature uptime or trip-level accessibility.
The report does not attribute ridership, safety, reliability, or customer outcomes to the projects.
records.next_action: Track each named station through final completion, compliant features, entrance and platform availability, outages, service use, and rider experience.

records.title: Amtrak records eight final station completions in the six-month cohort
records.finding: Amtrak reports eight named station projects reached final completion between November 1, 2025 and April 30, 2026.
records.denominator: Eight named final-completion projects in the reporting window: Albany, Camden, Columbus, Detroit Lakes, Devils Lake, Fort Morgan, Mount Pleasant, and Tomah.
evidence_limits: Final project completion is not a measure of feature uptime after turnover.
The final-completion list does not state which station elements changed in each location.
No rider, ridership, safety, reliability, or cost outcome is reported for the cohort.
records.next_action: Add project-specific scope, acceptance date, compliant features, outages, maintenance, service use, and rider-level outcomes for the same eight locations.

records.title: Three Amtrak stations appear in both passenger-use and final-completion cohorts
records.finding: FTFN reconciles Amtrak's two named lists and finds Camden, Detroit Lakes, and Fort Morgan in both the substantial-completion and final-completion cohorts for the same six-month reporting window.
records.denominator: The exact intersection of the report's eleven-station substantial-completion list and eight-station final-completion list: three named stations.

records.finding: ConnectLA reports that Nextlink activated a BEAD-funded fixed-wireless tower on May 1, 2026 and made gigabit-speed service available to 104 BEAD locations in Bossier Parish.

records.title: Hanford ETF treats 7.25 million gallons in a six-month campaign
records.finding: DOE reports that the Effluent Treatment Facility processed more than 7.25 million gallons of contaminated wastewater over six months and lowered one storage-basin level by almost 17 feet.
records.denominator: One six-month ETF campaign, measured as treated wastewater volume and the separate level change in one named storage basin.
evidence_limits: Treated volume is not contaminant mass removed or restored environmental condition.
The basin-level change is not a sitewide inventory or capacity measure.
No influent and effluent concentration, quality yield, downtime, energy, unit cost, or independent validation is disclosed.
records.next_action: Add compatible ETF campaigns with feed source, influent and effluent concentrations, contaminant mass, quality, uptime, energy, unit cost, basin inventory, and regulator review.

records.title: Hanford treats 2.3 billion groundwater gallons in FY 2024, the tenth year above 2 billion
records.finding: DOE reports 2.3 billion gallons treated in FY 2024 and ten consecutive fiscal years above 2 billion gallons, while Washington Ecology later reports more than 38 billion gallons cumulatively across six facilities.
records.denominator: FY 2024 sitewide treated groundwater volume across Hanford's six treatment systems, plus a ten-year threshold series; the later regulator cumulative total is a separate denominator.
